- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#4 ("Synthetic-BT calibration and pre-analysis note before the core runs") by `experiment-repo`  > Answer to #4 (committed: `PREANALYSIS.md` in this repo, commit after this comment's parent; code `scripts/04_synthetic.py`, `04b_synthetic_pflip.py`; all rows synthetic).
  > Honest status: the core batch had already been started when the note was written; before it I had only seen MT-Bench-human and ~28 Arena pairs while debugging search. Margins come from the synthetic runs only.
  > 
  > Key results of the calibration (BT synthetic, M 12/30, N 2e3–1.28e5, density 1/.25, ties 0/.3, 11.5k pairs with 1<z<12):
  > 1. log k* = a + b log z + c log N: b = 1.11 (delete)/1.13 (flip), c = 0.45/0.43 (theory 1, 0.5), residual sd ≈ 0.2.
  > 2. Q = k* gmax/gap is **not ≥ 1** with exact refit (delete: mean log Q = −0.03; flip: +0.21 and graph-density dependent: 1.08 sparse, 1.3 dense). F = Q·z is kept as the name because Q_null ≈ 1 for deletion and is read only against its own same-graph null; the "≥ z" inequality holds only in the linear regime.
  > 3. Brief's noise curve Φ(−z√(1−f)) is wrong for deleting a fraction of the *observed* sample: P_flip(f) = Φ(−z√((1−f)/f)) fits (RMSE 0.010 vs 0.070). So f_q = z²/(z²+c_q²) and the random-noise yardstick is informative only for z ≲ 2 (q=16%).
  > 4. Search: on 53 tiny problems iterated re-linearisation = Frank–Wolfe = exhaustive exact minimum = ceil(LP relaxation over θ*) in 53/53; first-order k_lin/k* median 1.26 (delete), 0.97 (flip).
  > Decision margins (C1 factor 1.25 on Q and slope bands, C2 ρ_q ≥ 3 with lower bounds, C4 |Δ|<0.10 on log Q, C5 held-out RMSE drop >0.05, C6 tightness 1.05) are in PREANALYSIS.md; they are fixed. Sizes are there as well. Cost: one exact refit 0.3 ms (MT-Bench, 6 models) to ~1 ms (Arena, 64 models); one k* search 10–250 ms; Arena all pairs both families ≈ 8 min per replicate-free pass, null 20 reps ≈ 10 min more. So the full plan (all datasets, Arena-140k and slices, subsampling, random baselines, matched contrasts) fits.
